attribution.note: Marcus explicitly describes his own views.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully isolates the statement's retrospective assertion about LLMs.

contract.note: Public access and downloadable models are an ordinary reading of the metaphor in a discussion of bad actors obtaining AI. The contract appropriately avoids requiring demonstrated harms.

evidence.note: Meta's dated company disclosure describes existing public assistant access and model downloads before the statement. It establishes release availability under the contract, not independent findings about safety.

reviews.rationale: The April 2024 release record establishes public LLM access and downloadable models before May 17. This satisfies the contract's fair plain reading; no contrary availability evidence is supplied.

attribution.note: Marcus presents the distinction between LLMs and AGI as his own view.

semantics.note: AGI not yet having been achieved is a reasonable ordinary reading of the retrospective contrast, although the metaphor supplies no operational definition.

contract.note: Broad, flexible human-level competence is a fair ordinary reading of AGI here. The chosen definition matters because weaker definitions admit emerging AGI; Marcus supplied no threshold. The reporting window is an evaluator choice.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous synthesis provides limited support through documented capability limitations. Partial proficiency and imperfect reliability do not establish that every frontier system fell below broad human-level competence.
This earlier research explains competing AGI definitions. It does not establish the May 2024 frontier's capabilities under the contract.

The earlier GPT-4 study offers a competing interpretation and selected human-level successes. Its incomplete-AGI characterization does not establish the contract's competence standard or the May 2024 state.

reviews.rationale: The plain reading is fair, but the packet does not settle it. The contemporary synthesis documents limitations without establishing the universal absence of qualifying AGI. Earlier emerging-AGI frameworks and GPT-4 demonstrations neither resolve the May 2024 state nor meet the contract's contradiction criterion.
